title: Testing strategy: unit, snapshot, UI tests and Swift Testing
summary: Have many fast unit tests for logic, some snapshot tests for UI components, a few integration tests, and a small number of UI tests for critical flows. Swift Testing is the modern unit-test framework; XCTest is still used for UI and performance tests.
body: **The testing pyramid:** bottom - lots of **unit tests** (view models, business rules, parsers) that run in milliseconds. Middle - **snapshot tests** (render a view and compare to a saved image) and **integration tests** (real components with a stubbed network). Top - a few **UI tests** (XCUITest) for flows like login and purchase; they are slow and flaky, so keep them few.
**Making code testable:** inject dependencies (API client, database, clock) through protocols or closures, so tests can use fakes. Keep logic out of views.
**Test doubles:** **stub** returns fixed data; **mock** also records how it was called so you can assert on it; **fake** is a working lightweight version (in-memory database).

**Swift Testing:** `@Test` functions, `#expect(a == b)`, `#require` (unwrap or stop), parameterized tests `@Test(arguments:)`, traits (`.tags`, `.timeLimit`, `.disabled`), suites are structs so each test gets fresh state, runs in parallel by default. Exit tests check code that crashes.
**Async tests:** mark the test `async` and `await`; inject a controllable clock instead of `sleep`; use `confirmation` for events that must happen.
**Flaky tests:** usually caused by shared state, real time, real network, or test order. Quarantine and fix; track flakiness automatically.
**Staff angle:** CI time budget, run only tests affected by a change on PRs, coverage as a signal not a target, ownership dashboards.
keyPoints: Pyramid: many unit tests, some snapshot/integration, few UI tests.
Dependency injection makes code testable; know stub vs mock vs fake.
Swift Testing: `@Test`, `#expect`, `#require`, parameterized, parallel by default.
Never sleep in tests; inject clocks.
Fight flakiness actively; keep CI fast.

mistakes: Testing private implementation details instead of behavior.
Hitting the real network in unit tests.
Lots of UI tests for things unit tests could cover.
followups: **How do you test a view model that calls an API?** Inject a fake API returning success/failure and assert the published state.
**How do you test code with `Date()` or timers?** Inject a date provider/clock.
**XCTest vs Swift Testing?** Swift Testing for new unit tests (better syntax, parallel, parameterized); XCTest still needed for UI and performance tests; both can live in one target.
